hcp.quadratic_conclusion: exact common isotropic quadratic form; leading diffusive covariance I/3

stacking_alignment.basis: FCC [1,-1,0]/sqrt(2) -> HCP x, FCC [1,1,1]/sqrt(3) -> HCP z, right-handed y
stacking_alignment.finite_scale_order: for k=xi/sqrt(n), n*log(lambda(k)) has quartic correction O(|xi|^4/n)
stacking_alignment.small_k_10e36_certificate: quartic FCC/HCP difference is bounded by O(10^-36) in the diffusive expansion; this is a local small-k statement only, not a global heat-kernel theorem

barlow_return_gauge_theorem.hypotheses: bi-infinite legal Barlow close-packed stacking; uniform 12-neighbor transition; ideal geometry; basal Fourier decomposition
barlow_return_gauge_theorem.fiber: (P_k psi)_j = C(k)/6 psi_j + t_j(k) psi_{j+1} + conjugate(t_{j-1}(k)) psi_{j-1}
barlow_return_gauge_theorem.hopping: t_j(k)=S_sigma_j(k)/12, sigma_j in {+,-}; S_-(k)=conjugate(S_+(k)) up to the fixed orientation convention and |S_sigma|=sqrt(3+2*C(k))
barlow_return_gauge_theorem.proof: the layer graph is Z, hence has no cycle flux. For nonzero hopping choose u_0=1 and recursively choose unit phases u_{j+1} so conjugate(u_j)*t_j*u_{j+1}=|t_j|. At zeros set the phase arbitrarily because the edge vanishes. The diagonal unitary U_k fixes delta_0 and converts every fiber to the same real constant-magnitude Jacobi fiber. The phase choice can be made measurable in k, so the direct-integral unitary is valid.
exact_consequences: same root return probability for every n and every legal Barlow stacking
same root local spectral measure for every legal Barlow stacking
same infinite-operator spectrum under the direct-integral unitary
barlow_return_gauge_theorem.integrated_DOS_boundary: periodic stackings inherit the same integrated DOS exactly. For arbitrary nonperiodic stackings, equality holds for any standard IDS definition obtained from the common local spectral measure when the IDS/trace-per-volume limit exists; existence is a separate assumption and is not asserted here.
barlow_return_gauge_theorem.does_not_preserve: the gauge is k-dependent and is not a physical-coordinate vertex permutation; it does not erase wavevector-labelled angular dispersion, local cubic/quartic stacking memory, or pointwise finite-time heat-kernel differences
